advances: This is an exact product counterexample to using only the change in the continuous sharp factor to compensate a deleted integrality test. The coarse measure is intrinsic and the actual fine target has integer rank $4r$.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The accepted single-diamond depth fact supplies its full-dimensional lifted hull, exact fine and coarse base traces, and singleton height on each coarse integer base. Since $\operatorname{conv}(T_r)=(\operatorname{conv}T')^r$, each assertion about traces and lifted heights takes Cartesian products. This gives the stated coarse and fine counts, the full dimension, and the generating fine fibers. Their common intrinsic volume is $V$, while the full coarse volume of each graph-height fiber is zero.

For the fine lower bound, the centroid in any one fiber pays $\Gamma_s V$ from that fiber by 6a7d56e450b3126f at zero shift, or pays $V$ if the restriction is constant. For the coarse lower bound, use the five-point diamond in each factor. Its lifted sites are centrally symmetric about $\widehat p_2=(p_2,1/2)$ by the two disjoint lifted midpoint identities in 358113ce6a951053. The product of these five-point sets has $5^r$ sites centrally symmetric about the tuple of centers. At its center mark with continuous coordinate $c_K$, restrict attention to these $5^r$ fibers. For a nonzero simplex-coordinate normal, the conditional scalar margin is the centered simplex marginal plus the independent symmetric scalar displacement from the uniform lifted base on that finite product. Its cap probability is at least $\Gamma_s$ by the paired-tail inequality of 6a7d56e450b3126f after conditioning on the opposite displacements. For zero simplex-coordinate normal, the centered closed cap takes at least half that subsource by symmetry, which is at least $\Gamma_s$ since $(1+1/s)^s\ge2$. All containing caps include their parallel through-mark versions. The coarse lower bound is therefore $\Gamma_s5^rV/(10^rV)$.

For the matching upper bounds, use the single-factor exposure penalties from the proof of 358113ce6a951053. Over each noncentral site $p_i$ choose a base affine function $a_i\ge0$ on $P'$, zero only at $p_i$, with gap at least one at all other sites. A supporting functional exposing $p_i$ among the nine vertices has a strict gap also at $p_2$, since $p_2$ is the midpoint of one of the two opposite pairs omitting $p_i$, and rescaling gives gap one. For $p_2$ use $a_2(p)=y(p)$, zero on the five diamond sites and at least one at the other integer sites. For any coarse base tuple with $k$ central factors, the sum $A$ of its factor penalties has exactly $5^k$ zero sites and gap at least one elsewhere. If $\lambda_j$ are the simplex barycentric coordinates, the $s+1$ caps
$$
\lambda_j(x)-1/(s+1)-2A\ge0
$$
cover the entire target fiber, because $A=0$ there and some $\lambda_j(x)\ge1/(s+1)$. They capture the corresponding simplex cap at each zero site, of volume $\Gamma_s V$ by homothety about vertex $j$, and none elsewhere since $\lambda_j\le1$. Each cap therefore has coarse mass $5^k\Gamma_sV\le5^r\Gamma_sV$. For a fine tuple all factors are noncentral, and the same argument isolates the one target fine fiber. The matching upper bounds hold at every mark in their respective sources. The depth ratio and retained mass fraction now follow by division.

For the proxy comparison, let $f(t)=\log\bigl[(t/(t+1))^t\bigr]$ for $t>0$. Direct differentiation gives $f''(t)=1/[t(t+1)^2]>0$. Thus the successive ratios $\Gamma_{j+1}/\Gamma_j$ are strictly increasing over positive integers and start at $8/9$. Multiplication gives $\Gamma_{s+r}/\Gamma_s\ge(8/9)^r$, with equality exactly for $s=r=1$. Dividing the actual fine depth by the proxy gives $(8/9)^r\Gamma_s/\Gamma_{s+r}\to0$ for fixed $s$, since $\Gamma_t\to e^{-1}$. Finally $9^r<16^r$ for $r\ge1$.

statement:
Use the ten-point diamond base $P'$, height $g$, and fine base $T'$ with the indexing of accepted fact 358113ce6a951053. For integers $r,s\ge1$ put $T_r=(T')^r$, and let $K$ be an $s$-simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $c_K$. The body $C=\operatorname{conv}(T_r)\times K$ is full-dimensional in $\mathbb R^{4r+s}$ and is the convex hull of its actual fine source. Its fine source with all $4r$ base coordinates integral consists of $9^r$ copies of $K$. Its coarse source with only the $3r$ original base coordinates integral consists of $10^r$ copies of $K$ at their prescribed heights, of intrinsic $\mathcal H_s$ mass $10^rV$ and full coarse $(s+r)$-volume zero. With $\Gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$, the respective normalized closed-halfspace maximum depths are $\Gamma_s/9^r$ and $\Gamma_s/2^r$. The coarse maximum is attained at the tuple of fractional-height diamond centers with continuous coordinate $c_K$. The fine/coarse depth ratio is $(2/9)^r$ and the retained intrinsic mass fraction is $(9/10)^r$.

The fine depth is at most $\Gamma_{s+r}/8^r$, with equality exactly for $s=r=1$, and its ratio to this proxy tends to zero as $r\to\infty$ with $s$ fixed. The actual fine-rank target $\Gamma_s/16^r$ is strictly below the fine depth.
title: The diamond filter has exact coarse and fine depths under products
